This is an application seeking pre-arrest bail filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.290 of 2024 of Ottapalam Police Station, Palakkad registered alleging offences punishable under sections 498A and 306 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860.
3.

According to the prosecution, on 03.03.2024, between 2.45 pm and 3 pm, the daughter of the defacto complainant by name Fathimathul Aneesha committed suicide by hanging from the fan in a bed room and the accused abetted the commission of the said offence.
4. Sri. Abhilash N., the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the prosecution allegations are false and the petitioner has no involvement in the commission of suicide by his wife.

It was also submitted that petitioner was residing abroad at the time of her suicide and that the mother of the deceased has even filed an affidavit stating that she has no objection in granting anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

5. Sri. K.A. Noushad, the learned Public Prosecutor on the other hand 2025:KER:58980 submitted that the investigation conducted so far has revealed that petitioner had abetted the commission of suicide and that there were matrimonial disputes between them and she committed suicide immediately after attending a call from the petitioner and hence custodial interrogation is necessary.
6. I have considered the rival contentions and have also perused the case diary.
7. Petitioner and the deceased married on 20.12.2020.
Petitioner has been working in the Gulf and he comes home only occasionally during holidays.
Petitioner and the victim were in contact with each other over phone everyday.
The mother of the deceased has given a statement that there were constant fights between both of them over phone and that the deceased often looked upset after the telephone call.
Despite the above, the defacto complainant has stated that the relationship between the petitioner and the deceased were cordial and that they had no knowledge about any acrimony between them.

2 8.
Squabbles in a married life are quite normal.
Minor skirmishes, difference of opinions, varying likes and dislikes between couples are all quotidian.
However, as Shakespeare wrote "Our remedies oft in ourselves do lie", it is upon each couple to find solutions to those problems, not by taking the extreme step, but by other means.

Merely because one of the spouses to a marriage committed suicide due to an inability to resolve the acrimony between them, that by itself cannot categorize the other spouse as having abetted the commission of suicide, especially in the absence of any other material.
The scope of the term abetment is distinct.
Inability of the spouses to resolve conflicts in a marriage cannot be a reason to assume that 2025:KER:58980 the other spouse had induced the deceased to commit suicide.
9. The offence of abetment of suicide under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'the BNS') requires the ingredients of Section 45 of the BNS to be satisfied.
As per the said provision, a person abets the doing of a thing, if he instigates any person to do that thing or intentionally aids the doing of that thing.
It is not every act or conduct that may amount to abetment of suicide.
Law requires the accused to have intended by his act or instigation that the deceased would commit suicide.
In order to attract the offence under Section 108 of the BNS, the abetment must have been for committing suicide and not for doing some other act.

Unless the instigation is done with the intention to prod the deceased to commit suicide, or had intentionally aided the commission of suicide, the offence under Section 108 of the BNS will not be attracted.
The crucial ingredient of the offence of abetment of suicide is the element of mens rea in prompting the deceased to commit suicide.
In other words, the act alleged as instigation must have been done with the intention that the deceased had to commit suicide.
Hence the essence of the offence of abetment of suicide is not what the deceased felt, but what the accused intended.
10. In this context, it is appropriate to mention that a straight - jacket formula cannot be adopted while dealing with cases of abetment of suicide.

In the decision in Radhika Kapahita (Dr.) v. State of Kerala [2024 (2) KLT 635] it was observed that the essence of the offence of abetment of suicide is not what the deceased felt, but what the accused intended and also that no straight - jacket formula can be adopted while dealing with cases of abetment of suicide as each case had to be 2025:KER:58980 decided on the basis of its own facts and circumstances.

State of Punjab, [(2004) 13 SCC 129] that, "Abetment involves a mental process of instigating a person or intentionally aiding that person in doing of a thing.

A more active role which can be described as instigating or aiding the doing of a thing is required before a person can be said to be abetting the commission of offence under S.306 IPC."
12.
In the instant case, except for the suicide note, prima facie, there are no materials to indicate abetment of commission of suicide by the accused.
Even if the suicide note is taken into consideration, it will only suggest that there were certain disputes between the parties.

that by itself cannot lead to the conclusion that the accused had abetted the commission of suicide.

13.
In view of the above, it is evident that the petitioner ought not to be subjected to custodial interrogation and is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail.
However, considering the nature of allegations, I am of the view that the petitioner must subject himself for interrogation for the purpose of completing the investigation.

Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 13.08.2025 and shall subject himself to interrogation from 10 AM to 5 PM, which period shall be treated as limited custody.

(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioner,
then, he shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.

(d) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses;
nor shall he tamper with the evidence.
(e) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.
